title: SDK transition: deprecation matrix, canonical migration examples, and changelog automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Produce a concise deprecation matrix for v1->v2 SDK breaking changes across Python/TypeScript/Go, author canonical migration snippets for common patterns (retries, streaming, structured outputs), and implement an automated changelog generator that pulls PR metadata + compatibility notes. The output artifacts: (1) deprecation matrix CSV/JSON for product/console consumption, (2) canonical 'recipes' page with minimal copy-paste snippets for engineers, (3) a CI job that compiles PR labels and @reviewer notes into a changelog draft. This ticket covers docs + CI glue + review loop, not the runtime SDK changes themselves.
acceptance_criteria: A single deprecation matrix (flat CSV) listing v1 API -> v2 replacement, migration risk, recommended urgency (now/next/optional), and test examples

Canonical migration recipe page exists in docs with at least 8 examples: init/auth, sync->streaming, retry/backoff, error types, embeddings signature, function-calling changes, typed responses, and Go context propagation

Changelog automation GH action produces a draft markdown file in .changelogs/ with entries from merged PRs labeled 'sdk-breaking' and includes: PR link, author, brief human-friendly migration hint, files changed list
Docs reviewed by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Design review for example ergonomics
Unit/regression tests for 3 canonical migration snippets (smoke tests) run in CI and pass
tasks: Inventory: scan merged SDK PRs since 2024-01 for breaking-change labels (automation script)
Draft deprecation matrix CSV and JSON outputs
Write canonical migration recipes for Python, TypeScript, and Go (8 examples)
Design review: example UX and recommended idiomatic patterns
Implement GitHub Action 'sdk-changelog-builder' that aggregates PR metadata and composes draft changelog
Add smoke tests executing minimal migration snippets in build matrix
Stakeholder review session: present matrix and recipes to SDK and Docs teams
Finalize docs page and wire to docs search/redirects
examples:
# v1 pattern (pseudo)
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=OLD_KEY)
resp = client.generate('Hello')
# v2 pattern
from redwood import Client, RetryPolicy
client = Client(api_key=NEW_KEY, retry=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=4, backoff='exponential'))
resp = client.text.generate('Hello')
Retry differences: v1 used max_retries int on client; v2 uses RetryPolicy with jittered exponential backoff and idempotency token guidance
Streaming differences: v2 splits 'delta' (token diffs) from 'meta' (tool/function calls) and recommends consumers ignore empty-delta keep-alive frames
streaming_ergonomics_notes: Recommendation: provide high-level helpers in each SDK for common streaming patterns: 'to_string(stream)', 'to_async_iter(stream)' and 'with_progress(stream, on_update)'. Docs include best-practice for partial result concatenation, handling function/tool call frames, and rehydrating KV cache positions when reconnecting.
retries_policy_diff: Summary: v1 exposed primitive retries (count + fixed backoff). v2 standardizes RetryPolicy: {max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, multiplier, jitter_kind, idempotency_strategies}. Migration recipe: map old count -> max_attempts, set multiplier 1.6, initial backoff 100ms, jitter 'full', and document endpoints requiring idempotency token (e.g., fine-tune/upload endpoints).
changelog_automation_plan: Create GH Action that triggers on label 'sdk-breaking' or on release branch merges
Action collects PR title, number, author, files changed (filter to /sdk/), and first doc reference in PR body
Use a small templates/CHANGELOG_SNIPPET.md to render human-friendly migration hint (maintainers fill the hint in PR body under 'Migration Hint:'),
Action commits draft to .changelogs/draft-<release>.md and opens PR to docs repo for review
Add unit test to assert that any PR labeled 'sdk-breaking' includes a 'Migration Hint' section
